title: Recurring-event corrections (series + instance) + mailto fallback
description: # Recurring-event corrections + mailto fallback ## Context The public corrections feature (built earlier this session) only works against `EVENT#{guid}` rows. Recurring events were explicitly out of scope: an occurrence's `guid` is a hash recomputed fresh from the series' title/time/url on every site build — it's not a stable, persisted identity, so nothing could safely be targeted by it. The "Report an issue" link on `event_page.html` is currently hidden entirely for recurring occurrences as a result. The user wants recurring events correctable too — both the series definition itself (e.g. the venue is wrong for the whole weekly meetup) and a single occurrence (e.g. this one date moved). They also want a small generic mailto fallback on every event page, recurring or not. Decided with the user: build both series-level and instance-level corrections now (not phased), and the public-correctable field set for either is `('description', 'location', 'url', 'time')` — the same fields already allowed on a non-iCal event, minus `end_time` (which doesn't exist on recurring definitions). ## Approach Reuse the entire existing `CORRECTION#` pending→approve/reject pipeline, generalized with a `target_type` discriminator (`'event' | 'recurring_series' | 'recurring_instance'`) instead of building a parallel system. Two different apply mechanisms on approval, chosen deliberately for their actual concurrency profile: - **Series-level**: merge `fields` directly onto the `RECURRING#{slug}` record's top-level attributes — the same full merge-and-replace the MCP `update_recurring_event` tool already does by hand. No `_rev`/overlay/audit machinery: the only two writers of a RECURRING# record are that trusted MCP tool and now approved corrections, both low-frequency and one-at-a-time via a human review queue — much lower race risk than EVENT# overlays, which arbitrate the QA agent, admin hand-edits, and corrections all potentially concurrently. This also means **no calgen pipeline change is needed for series-level** — `load_recurring_events()` just picks up whatever's on the record, same as an admin edit. - **Instance-level**: a new persisted entity, `PK=RECURRING#{slug}` / `SK=OVERRIDE#{date}` — same partition as the series definition (a single-table "definition plus its dated children" query), keyed by `(slug, date)` rather than the occurrence's ephemeral guid, since that guid isn't safe to target (a base-definition edit silently changes it on the next build). Same last-write-wins simplification as above. Occurrence identity for correction purposes is always `(recurring_slug, date)`, never the guid. `event.id` already carries the recurring slug through calgen's pipeline by coincidence, not by design — give it an explicit name (`recurring_slug`) rather than building on the ambiguous one. Frontend: generalize the existing `correct-event.html`/`correction.js` to handle all three target types (via `?guid=`, `?recurring=slug`, or `?recurring=slug&date=`), rather than forking a third near-duplicate magic-link form — `submission.js`/`correction.js`'s magic-link code is already flagged as a separate duplication cleanup item; a third copy would make that worse, not better. The series-vs-instance choice is a toggle inside the form itself ("This applies to every occurrence, not just this date"), shown only when arriving in instance mode, not two separate links on the event page. ### `cdk_next/lambda_src/api/db.py` New constants (next to `ICAL_CORRECTION_FIELDS`): ```python RECURRING_CORRECTION_FIELDS = ('description', 'location', 'url', 'time') CORRECTION_TARGET_TYPES = ('event', 'recurring_series', 'recurring_instance') ``` `correction_allowed_fields_for_target(target_type, source=None)` — dispatches to the existing `correction_allowed_fields(source)` for `'event'`, else returns `RECURRING_CORRECTION_FIELDS`. `check_correction_fields` signature changes from `(source, fields)` to `(target_type, fields, source=None)`. Update every call site: `routes/corrections.py`, `db.approve_correction`, and all direct calls in `test_corrections.py`. `create_correction` signature changes from `(target_guid, fields, reason, submitter_email, submitter_id=None)` to `(target_type, target_id, fields, reason, submitter_email, submitter_id=None, target_date=None)`. Branches: `'event'` → `get_event_from_config` (unchanged validation); `'recurring_series'`/`'recurring_instance'` → `get_recurring_event(target_id)`; `'recurring_instance'` additionally requires `target_date` (validate via the existing `validate_event_date(target_date, field='target_date')`, confirmed it already supports a custom `field=` label for error messages). Item gains `target_type`, `target_id`, `target_date` (instance only); keep writing `target_guid` too when `target_type == 'event'` as a back-compat alias. `_correction_item_to_dict` — add `target_type`/`target_id`/`target_date` to the read field list; if `target_type` is absent on an old row (written before this change), default it to `'event'` and backfill `target_id` from `target_guid` — no migration script needed, every existing row is test data anyway. `approve_correction` — three-way dispatch on `correction['target_type']` (default `'event'` for legacy rows): event path unchanged (`set_event_overlay`); `recurring_series` re-validates fields then calls the new `merge_recurring_event_fields(slug, fields)`; `recurring_instance` re-validates then calls the new `set_recurring_instance_override(slug, date, fields, comment, actor=reviewer_email)`. Every "target gone" message keeps the substring `no longer exists` and every "already resolved" message keeps `already` — `routes/corrections.py`'s existing `_resolve_error` string-matching needs no changes. New helper (used by both the approval path and, optionally, a refactored `update_recurring_event` MCP tool): ```python def merge_recurring_event_fields(slug, fields): event = get_recurring_event(slug) if not event: raise ValueError(f'No such recurring event: {slug}') data = {k: v for k, v in event.items() if k != 'id'} data.update(fields) put_recurring_event(slug, data) return data ``` New instance-override storage, next to `get_all_recurring_events`/`delete_recurring_event`: ```python def set_recurring_instance_override(slug, date, fields, comment=None, *, actor=None): date = validate_event_date(date, field='date') if not date: raise ValueError('date is required') existing = get_recurring_instance_override(slug, date) or {} merged = dict(existing) merged.update(dict(fields)) if 'url' in merged and not is_safe_url(merged.get('url')): merged['url'] = '' merged['_edited_by'] = actor or 'agent:mcp' merged['_edited_at'] = _now_iso() if comment: merged['_comment'] = comment table = _get_table() item = {'PK': f'RECURRING#{slug}', 'SK': f'OVERRIDE#{date}', **{k: _from_plain(v) for k, v in merged.items()}} table.put_item(Item=item) return _instance_override_item_to_dict(item) def get_recurring_instance_override(slug, date): table = _get_table() response = table.get_item(Key={'PK': f'RECURRING#{slug}', 'SK': f'OVERRIDE#{date}'}) item = response.get('Item') return _instance_override_item_to_dict(item) if item else None def get_recurring_instance_overrides(slug): """{date: {field: value}} for every override under this series.""" table = _get_table() items = _query_all(table, KeyConditionExpression=( Key('PK').eq(f'RECURRING#{slug}') & Key('SK').begins_with('OVERRIDE#'))) return {item['SK'].split('#', 1)[1]: _instance_override_item_to_dict(item) for item in items} def delete_recurring_instance_override(slug, date): table = _get_table() table.delete_item(Key={'PK': f'RECURRING#{slug}', 'SK': f'OVERRIDE#{date}'}) def _instance_override_item_to_dict(item): return {k: _to_plain(v) for k, v in item.items() if k not in ('PK', 'SK') and not k.startswith('GSI')} ``` `get_corrections_by_status`/`get_corrections_by_submitter` need **no changes** — their existing `item['PK'].startswith('CORRECTION#')` collision filter (guarding against the DRAFT#/CORRECTION# GSI1 collision fixed earlier this session) is a key-attribute check, unrelated to `target_type`. ### `cdk_next/lambda_src/api/routes/corrections.py` `submit_correction_json` — reads `target_type` (default `'event'`), `target_id` (falls back to `guid` for back-compat), `target_date`. Validates target exists per type before calling `db.check_correction_fields`/`db.create_correction`. New `get_public_recurring_json(event, jinja_env, slug)` — `GET /api/public/recurring/{slug}?date=YYYY-MM-DD`. Returns the series' base correctable values always; if `?date=` is given, also returns that occurrence's *effective* values (series merged with any existing override for that date) so the form corrects against what's actually showing — same reasoning `get_public_event_json` already documents. `date` does **not** need to be a currently-in-window rrule occurrence (a correction against a date that's aged out of the 90-day expansion window must still be submittable). `get_correction_json` (admin) — enrichment branches: event → unchanged; recurring targets → `db.get_recurring_event(target_id)`, plus `db.get_recurring_instance_override(...)` for instance targets. `approve_correction_json`/`reject_correction_json`/`_resolve_error` — no changes. ### `cdk_next/lambda_src/api/handler.py` + `cdk_next/stacks/api_stack.py` `handler.py` — new route, next to the existing `/api/public/events/` block: ```python if path.startswith('/api/public/recurring/') and http_method == 'GET': slug = path[len('/api/public/recurring/'):].split('/')[0] if slug: return add_cors(corrections.get_public_recurring_json(event, jinja_env, slug)) ``` `api_stack.py` — `/api/admin/*` needs nothing (already a CDK proxy). The `public` resource is NOT proxied (explicit children only), so add a sibling resource next to the existing `public_res.add_resource("events")...` line: ```python public_res.add_resource("recurring").add_resource("{slug}").add_method("GET", integration) ``` Unauthenticated at the gateway, matching `public/events/{guid}`. ### `packages/calgen/src/calgen/pipeline.py` `overlay.py` needs **no change** — `apply_overlay`'s field gate is a denylist (`OVERLAY_PROTECTED_FIELDS`), not tied to the EVENT# allowlist; none of `description`/`location`/`url`/`time` are protected, so it already merges these correctly for any caller. `expand_recurring_events` gains `instance_overrides=None` (shape `{slug: {date: {field: value}}}`). Inside the loop, after computing `instance['date']`/`instance['guid']`, call `apply_overlay(instance, instance_overrides.get(event.get('id'), {}).get(instance['date']))`. Guid stays computed *before* the overlay is applied — identity stays pre-correction-derived, consistent with why corrections must never target it. `process_events` gains `recurring_overrides=None`, threaded straight into `expand_recurring_events(..., instance_overrides=recurring_overrides)`. **Delete** the old dead call and its comment (`apply_overlay(occurrence, event_overrides.get(occurrence.get('guid')))` — confirmed always a no-op since `event_overrides` is only ever keyed by EVENT# guids). New loader `load_recurring_overlays()` (mirrors `load_overlays()`), reading `_recurring_overlay/{slug}.yaml` files into `{slug: {date: {field: value}}}`. Add `RECURRING_OVERLAY_DIR = '_recurring_overlay'` next to `OVERLAY_DIR`. Wire into `main()`: `recurring_overrides = load_recurring_overlays()`, passed into `process_events(...)`. No `cli.py` change needed — `calgen pipeline` calls `pipeline.main()` directly. Series-level corrections need no pipeline change at all: they're merged onto the RECURRING# record before `load_recurring_events()` ever runs, so every occurrence picks them up for free via `instance = dict(event)` — and because the instance-override `apply_overlay` call runs *after* that copy, an instance override naturally wins over a series-level value for its own date (more-specific-wins falls straight out of the existing copy-then-overlay order, no extra logic needed). Also add one line to `load_recurring_events()` right after `event['id'] = os.path.splitext(filename)[0]`: ```python event['recurring_slug'] = event['id'] ``` Purely additive — gives templates a self-documenting name instead of overloading `id`. ### `cdk_next/lambda_src/site_generator/export_dynamo_to_calgen.py` **Important, verified against the actual file**: the fix is not in the `_recurring_events/` loop — it's one level up. The table scan itself is filtered table-wide: `items = _scan_all(table, FilterExpression=Attr('SK').eq('META'))` (line 86). A new `SK='OVERRIDE#{date}'` item is invisible to the exporter entirely until that filter is broadened: ```python items = _scan_all(table, FilterExpression=( Attr('SK').eq('META') | Attr('SK').begins_with('OVERRIDE#'))) ``` Then the existing `_recurring_events/` loop must skip non-`META` rows (they'll now be mixed into `by_prefix['RECURRING']`): ```python for item in by_prefix.get('RECURRING', []): if item.get('SK') != 'META': continue ... ``` New export step right after it, one file per series (not per date, since a series can accumulate many dated overrides): ```python _reset_dir('_recurring_overlay') overrides_by_slug = {} for item in by_prefix.get('RECURRING', []): sk = item.get('SK', '') if not sk.startswith('OVERRIDE#'): continue slug = item['PK'].split('#', 1)[1] override_date = sk.split('#', 1)[1] fields = {k: v for k, v in _clean(item).items() if not k.startswith('_')} if fields: overrides_by_slug.setdefault(slug, {})[override_date] = fields for slug, by_date in overrides_by_slug.items(): _write_yaml(os.path.join('_recurring_overlay', f'{slug}.yaml'), by_date) ``` ### Frontend `frontends/edit/js/correction.js` — replace `readGuid()` with `readTarget()` recognizing three querystring shapes (`?guid=`, `?recurring=&date=` → instance, `?recurring=` alone → series). `fetchEvent` branches between `/api/public/events/{guid}` and `/api/public/recurring/{slug}?date=...`, normalizing both into the same `{correctable_fields, values, title}` shape the rest of the module already renders from. Show the series-toggle checkbox only in instance mode; on submit, flipping it changes the posted `target_type` from `recurring_instance` to `recurring_series` (dropping `target_date`). `requestLink`'s `redirect_path` must reconstruct whichever querystring got the visitor there, not hardcode `?guid=`. `frontends/edit/correct-event.html` — add the hidden-by-default series-toggle markup inside the form, update the `#not-correctable` copy (recurring events are no longer categorically uncorrectable), add the mailto fallback line under the subtitle. `site/templates/event_page.html` (~lines 107-115) — always show the "Report an issue" link now; recurring occurrences link to `?recurring={{ event.recurring_slug }}&date={{ event.date }}`, others keep `?guid={{ event.guid }}`. Add a generic mailto link next to it on every page: ```jinja · Email us directly ``` `ross@karchner.com` confirmed as the established contact point — matches `REPLY_TO_EMAIL`/`ADMIN_EMAIL` defaults in `routes/submit.py`, `NEWSLETTER_ADMIN_EMAIL` in `config.py`, and the address already hardcoded in `correct-event.html`'s existing fallback message. `frontends/edit/js/corrections.js` (admin queue) — generalize the `target_guid`-based row label and same-target conflict-grouping key to branch on `target_type` (series/instance show the slug + date, event shows the title as today). ### `cdk_next/lambda_src/mcp/server.py` `list_pending_corrections`/`get_correction`/`reject_correction`/`approve_correction` need no code changes — thin id-based wrappers, richer dicts flow through automatically. Optional polish (not required): route `update_recurring_event`'s inline merge logic through the new `db.merge_recurring_event_fields`. ## Edge cases (all confirmed to fall out of the design above, not bolted on) 1. **Correction for a date outside the 90-day window** — fully storable/approvable regardless (only date *format* is validated); it just produces an override row `expand_recurring_events` won't emit anything for until that date re-enters the window on a future build. 2. **Series correction approved after instance overrides exist for specific dates** — instance overrides still win for their date; falls straight out of copy-then-overlay ordering, no special-case code needed. 3. **Recurring series deleted between submission and approval** — `approve_correction` raises `'... no longer exists'`, correction stays `pending` (not auto-rejected), same as the existing event path. 4. **Concurrent writes to the same `(slug, date)` override** — explicitly accepted as last-write-wins, stated in the docstrings, matching the same reasoning already applied to series-level merges. 5. **Legacy `CORRECTION#` rows with no `target_type`** — handled entirely at read time (`_correction_item_to_dict` defaults to `'event'`), no migration needed. ## Verification **Unit tests** — update all `check_correction_fields`/`create_correction` call sites in `test_corrections.py` for the new signatures, then add coverage for: recurring-series field allowlist (accepts description/location/url/time, rejects rrule/categories), unknown-series/missing-target_date validation errors, series approval merges directly onto the record (no `overrides`/`_rev` introduced), instance approval writes a scoped override row, a second instance correction for the same date merges rather than replaces, approval against a deleted series raises and stays pending, and a regression test confirming `get_corrections_by_status` still excludes DRAFT# rows with recurring targets present. Both `FakeTable.query` implementations (`test_corrections.py` and `test_correction_routes.py`) need to handle a compound `Key(...).eq(...) & Key(...).begins_with(...)` condition for `get_recurring_instance_overrides` — verified the real shape: `type(cond).__name__ == 'And'`, `cond._values` is a 2-tuple of sub-conditions, each with `._values[0].name`/`._values[1]`. New `test_recurring_instance_overrides.py`: set/get a single override, setting twice merges rather than replaces, `get_recurring_instance_overrides` returns all dates for a series without collision across series, URL sanitization matches `put_recurring_event`'s. **calgen tests** — new `test_recurring_instance_overlay.py` mirroring `test_overlay.py`'s structure: a series-level edit shows on every occurrence, an instance override applies only to its own date, an instance override wins over a series-level value for its date (the concrete edge-case-2 regression), an override for a now-out-of-window date produces no occurrence but doesn't error, and protected fields are never merged (parametrized over `OVERLAY_PROTECTED_FIELDS`, matching the existing pattern in `test_overlay.py`). Confirm `test_overlay.py`'s existing `_run()` helper stays passing unmodified — the new `recurring_overrides=None` parameter is backward compatible with its current keyword-only call style. **End-to-end via API/MCP, once deployed**: submit a `recurring_series` correction (e.g. location) and a `recurring_instance` correction (e.g. description for one date) via MCP or magic-link curl against a real recurring series; confirm both appear in `GET /api/admin/corrections?status=pending` with the right `target_type`/`target_id`/`target_date`; approve each; confirm directly via `get_recurring_event`/`get_recurring_instance_override`; trigger a rebuild and confirm on the live site that the location correction shows on every occurrence while the description correction shows only on its one date. **End-to-end via a real browser (Playwright), mirroring how the original corrections feature was verified this session**: use a throwaway MCP-created recurring test event (delete it afterward) plus a temporary Cognito admin user (`aws cognito-idp admin-create-user`/`admin-set-user-password`, deleted afterward) for the admin-queue half, and a self-generated magic-link token (`aws kms generate-mac` against the deployed `SUBMIT_KEY_ID`, verified live rather than assumed — confirm the current key id from the Lambda's environment rather than trusting a remembered one, since that's bitten this session before) for the public-submission half. Steps: 1. Navigate to a recurring occurrence's live event page; confirm the "Report an issue" link now renders (previously suppressed) with the `?recurring=...&date=...` querystring, and the mailto link is present and correctly encoded. 2. Navigate to `/edit/correct-event.html?recurring=...&date=...` with a valid magic-link token in the URL; confirm the form loads the occurrence's current effective values, the series-toggle checkbox is present, and the correctable fields match `description/location/url/time` only (no `end_time`, no title/categories). 3. Submit an instance-level correction (toggle unchecked) with a distinct, greppable value; confirm success message. 4. Reload the same form fresh, submit again with the toggle checked (series-level) with a different distinct value; confirm success. 5. Sign in as the temporary Cognito admin, navigate to `/edit/corrections.html`; confirm both pending corrections render with correct labels (series shows slug, instance shows slug + date) and the conflict warning if both target the same series. 6. Approve the instance-level one, reject the series-level one (or vice versa) via the UI buttons; confirm the queue updates and reflects each outcome. 7. Trigger a rebuild; reload the occurrence page and a *different* occurrence of the same series in the browser; confirm the approved instance-level change shows only on its own date and the rejected series-level change shows nowhere. 8. Clean up: delete the test recurring event/overrides via MCP, delete the temporary Cognito user, revert/delete any stray CORRECTION# test rows via `reject_correction`/direct cleanup so the admin queue is left empty. ### Critical files - `cdk_next/lambda_src/api/db.py` - `cdk_next/lambda_src/api/routes/corrections.py` - `packages/calgen/src/calgen/pipeline.py` - `cdk_next/lambda_src/site_generator/export_dynamo_to_calgen.py` - `frontends/edit/js/correction.js`, `frontends/edit/correct-event.html` - `site/templates/event_page.html` - `cdk_next/lambda_src/api/test_corrections.py`

title: CORS wildcard fallback leaks to /api/admin/* responses
description: cdk_next/lambda_src/api/handler.py's get_cors_origin() returns '*' for any Origin outside the 3-item allowlist, and add_cors() applies this to every response including /api/admin/*. A comment claims it's 'restricted below' but no route actually narrows it back. Any site can read admin JSON responses from a browser holding a leaked/stolen bearer token. Fix: default-deny (no CORS header) instead of wildcard for unrecognized origins.
close_reason:
handler.py's get_cors_origin() now returns None (no ACAO header) for any origin outside ALLOWED_ORIGINS instead of falling back to '*'; add_cors() and the OPTIONS preflight both skip the header entirely when there's nothing to allow. Added test_handler.py covering allowlisted/unrecognized/missing-origin cases for both the direct helper and the OPTIONS branch. All 386 api tests pass.

While verifying live against the deployed API, found the same wildcard leak one layer up: api_stack.py's UNAUTHORIZED/ACCESS_DENIED gateway responses (API Gateway's own 401/403 for requests the Cognito authorizer rejects before Lambda runs) hardcoded Access-Control-Allow-Origin: '*' unconditionally — that path never goes through handler.py at all. Fixed by reflecting the caller's own Origin header (method.request.header.origin) instead of a literal wildcard; gateway responses can't run a real conditional allowlist check the way get_cors_origin() does, and these bodies are low-sensitivity (fixed "Unauthorized"/"Forbidden" text, no user data), so reflection here is a reasonable compromise that also keeps the legitimate dctech.events admin frontend able to read a 401 to show "please log in" rather than getting an opaque CORS failure.

Deployed NextApiStack and verified live via curl against both routes:
- /api/events (normal Lambda path): evil origin gets no ACAO header, dctech.events gets it echoed back correctly.
- /api/admin/corrections (401 via Cognito authorizer, gateway-response path): with cache-busting query strings (CloudFront — API Gateway EDGE endpoints sit behind an AWS-managed CloudFront distribution — was serving a stale cached copy of the pre-fix 401 for identical repeated URLs, which is expected default error-caching behavior and not a real residual issue), evil origin now gets its own origin reflected (not a blind '*'), dctech.events gets its own origin reflected, and a request with no Origin header at all gets no ACAO header.

title: SSRF risk: iCal aggregator fetches unvalidated URLs
description: packages/calgen/src/calgen/calendars.py (fetching group iCal URLs and scraped event page URLs) relies on db.py's is_safe_url(), which only rejects non-http(s) schemes -- http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/... or http://localhost/... pass through unchanged. A malicious or compromised group feed could trigger SSRF against the Lambda's metadata endpoint or internal network on every aggregator cycle. Fix: block private/link-local IP ranges, including after DNS resolution to stop DNS-rebinding, before fetching.
close_reason:
Added packages/calgen/src/calgen/ssrf_guard.py (safe_get) and wired it into calendars.py's two external fetch points: fetch_json_ld_data (Meetup page scraping) and fetch_ical_and_extract_events (group iCal feeds). Validates the resolved IP before connecting and rejects private/loopback/link-local/multicast/reserved/unspecified addresses (covers the metadata endpoint 169.254.169.254, localhost, RFC1918 ranges, etc).

Also closes the DNS-rebinding gap explicitly: the validating wrapper (a scoped socket.getaddrinfo patch) stays installed through the whole request, including requests/urllib3's own connection-time resolution and each redirect hop it manually follows — not just an up-front check — so a DNS answer that changes between the check and the actual connect is still caught rather than sailing through on the second, unguarded lookup.

Existing test_json_ld_event_types.py updated to mock the new safe_get call site instead of requests.get directly. New test_ssrf_guard.py covers: public addresses allowed, each private/internal IP class rejected, non-http(s) schemes rejected, a redirect to a private address rejected (and the private target never dialed), a redirect to a public address followed normally, the rebinding scenario (guard catches an unsafe address surfacing only on the connection-time lookup, after an earlier lookup for a different host already passed), too-many-redirects gives up, and the monkeypatch cleanly restores on both success and failure. Full calgen suite: 248 passed. Rebuilt Lambda assets and deployed NextIcalAggregatorStack (the actual scheduled consumer of fetch_ical_and_extract_events).

Scope note: left cdk_next/lambda_src/mcp/server.py's verify_ical_feed (admin-only MCP tool, human-triggered when adding a group) unguarded — same class of risk in principle, but lower severity (not an automatic third-party-controlled cycle) and would require pulling calgen into the mcp Lambda's dependencies just for this one function, which is more invasive than this bead's stated scope (calendars.py's automatic aggregator fetches). Worth a follow-up if it's ever worth the dependency.

title: Fix: CORRECTION# items leaked into the DRAFT# queue (GSI1/GSI3 collision)
description: get_drafts_by_status/get_drafts_by_submitter queried GSI1PK=STATUS#{status} / GSI3PK=USER#{id} with no PK-prefix filter, and CORRECTION# items (added by the corrections feature) use the identical convention -- a pending correction showed up in the admin Pending Submissions queue as an Untitled/no-details row, and clicking Reject 404'd ('Draft not found') because get_draft looks up PK=DRAFT#{id}, which doesn't exist for a correction stored at PK=CORRECTION#{id}. Found live in prod via user report + screenshot (queue.html showing a stuck 'Untitled' submission that couldn't be rejected). The corrections-side queries (get_corrections_by_status/by_submitter) already had the mirror-image filter; the drafts-side queries just never got the reverse fix. Fixed by adding the same item['PK'].startswith('DRAFT#') filter to both draft-query functions. 2 new regression tests in test_corrections.py. Full suite: 340 passing. Cleaned up the stray CORRECTION# item live via reject_correction.

title: Public corrections to published events
description: # Public corrections to published events ## Context Events on dctech.events come from three sources: an iCal feed (`source: 'ical'`), a manual entry, or a promoted public submission (`source: 'submitted'`). Once live, the only way to fix a wrong detail today is an admin hand-editing it in the `/edit/events.html` overlay UI — there's no way for a member of the public (an organizer, an attendee) to flag or fix something themselves. We want a lightweight "suggest a correction" path that lands in a moderation queue rather than writing directly to the live event, so nothing public-submitted goes live unreviewed. The one hard constraint: for iCal-sourced events, only `description`, venue (`location`), and `url` may be corrected — the date/time must stay whatever the iCal feed says, since that feed is the authoritative source and gets re-fetched independently. Investigating the existing overlay system (`db.py`'s `set_event_overlay`) turned up a useful fact: **`date`/`end_date` are already permanently un-overlayable for every event regardless of source** (`OVERLAY_PROTECTED_FIELDS`) — so date-locking needs no new code at all. The only field that actually needs new, source-conditional locking is `time`/`end_time`, which today *is* overlay-editable for every source, including iCal. Outcome: a public correction form linked from each event page, a moderation queue for admins to approve/reject, and — once approved — the correction is applied through the exact same `set_event_overlay` writer an admin hand-edit already uses, so there's no second code path for "how an event's displayed fields get changed." ## Approach A correction is a **new, separate pending entity** (`CORRECTION#{id}`), never written into an event's `overrides` until a moderator approves it. Approval is a thin wrapper around the existing `db.set_event_overlay(...)` — so once approved, a correction is indistinguishable from an admin hand-edit. Identity is handled by reusing `routes/submit.py`'s existing `_resolve_submitter` (magic link or Cognito) — no new auth code. The whole thing closely mirrors the existing DRAFT#/submission pipeline, reusing its shape wherever it fits rather than inventing a new pattern. ### Data model `CORRECTION#{uuid4[:8]}` item, modeled on `DRAFT#`'s shape (`db.py:255` `create_draft`): ``` PK: CORRECTION#{id} SK: META GSI1PK: STATUS#{status} GSI1SK: {created_at} # 'pending'|'approved'|'rejected' GSI3PK: USER#{submitter_id} GSI3SK: {created_at} target_guid, target_source (snapshot at submission), target_title (denormalized, cosmetic) fields: {field: new_value} # only changed fields, already allowlist- and type-checked reason: str # required — submitter's note on what's wrong submitter_email, submitter_id, created_at, status reviewer_email, reviewed_at, rejection_reason # set on resolution ``` **Important:** `DRAFT#` items already use the identical `GSI1PK = STATUS#{status}` / `GSI3PK = USER#{id}` convention. A query for `STATUS#pending` on GSI1 will return both drafts and corrections interleaved unless filtered. `db.py` already has this exact problem solved for `CANDIDATE#` items sharing GSI5 with `EVENT#` items — `get_candidates()` (db.py:1377-1384) post-filters on `item['PK'].startswith('CANDIDATE#')`. Do the same in `get_corrections_by_status`/`get_corrections_by_submitter`. ### Field allowlist (the core business rule) New constants in `db.py`, next to `OVERLAY_EDITABLE_FIELDS`/`OVERLAY_PROTECTED_FIELDS` (db.py:726-739): ```python ICAL_CORRECTION_FIELDS = ('description', 'location', 'url') OTHER_CORRECTION_FIELDS = ('description', 'location', 'url', 'time', 'end_time') CORRECTION_EDITABLE_FIELDS_BY_SOURCE = { 'ical': ICAL_CORRECTION_FIELDS, 'manual': OTHER_CORRECTION_FIELDS, 'submitted': OTHER_CORRECTION_FIELDS, } def correction_allowed_fields(source): # Unknown/future source values fall back to the narrower iCal set — fail # closed, not open. return CORRECTION_EDITABLE_FIELDS_BY_SOURCE.get(source, ICAL_CORRECTION_FIELDS) def check_correction_fields(source, fields): # Raises ValueError naming any field not in correction_allowed_fields(source). # Then reuses the existing _check_overlay_types(fields) so a correction can't # smuggle in a malformed value any more than an admin edit can. ``` `date`/`end_date` need no special-casing — already unconditionally rejected by `set_event_overlay`'s existing `OVERLAY_PROTECTED_FIELDS` check for every source. ### `db.py` additions (next to the DRAFT#/overlay functions, same reasoning as `build_event_draft_data` living there: `build_lambdas.sh` bundles `db.py` into the MCP Lambda but not the route modules) - `correction_allowed_fields(source)`, `check_correction_fields(source, fields)` — above. - `create_correction(target_guid, fields, reason, submitter_email, submitter_id=None)` — validates target exists via `get_event_from_config`, snapshots `source`/`title`, writes the item, returns the id. - `get_correction(correction_id)`, `get_corrections_by_status(status='pending')`, `get_corrections_by_submitter(user_id)` — mirror `get_draft`/`get_drafts_by_status`/`get_drafts_by_submitter`, with the PK-prefix filter noted above. - `approve_correction(correction_id, reviewer_email)` — fetches the correction, **re-fetches the target event live** (not the `target_source` snapshot) and re-runs `check_correction_fields` against its *current* source (an admin could have re-sourced the event since submission); raises `ValueError` if the event is gone or the fields are no longer all allowed, leaving the correction `pending` in either case (never auto-rejects on a transient failure). On success: `set_event_overlay(target_guid, fields, comment=f"Public correction from {submitter_email}: {reason}", actor=reviewer_email)` (default forgiving `expected_rev` — no live human to show a conflict to, same reasoning `set_event_overlay`'s own docstring gives for bulk/agent writes), then marks the correction `approved`. - `reject_correction(correction_id, reviewer_email, reason=None)` — marks `rejected`, no overlay write. ### Route layer: `cdk_next/lambda_src/api/routes/corrections.py` (new) Public: - `submit_correction_json` → `POST /api/corrections`. Reuses `_resolve_submitter` from `routes/submit.py` verbatim. Validates: guid present and resolves via `get_event_from_config` (404 if not); `fields` a non-empty dict; `reason` non-blank (required, mirroring `routes/events.py`'s non-empty-`comment` rule on the admin overlay endpoint); `check_correction_fields(source, fields)` (422 on `ValueError`). Then `create_correction(...)`, return 201 with the id. - `get_public_event_json` → `GET /api/public/events/{guid}` (**new endpoint** — there is no existing unauthenticated single-event read). Returns `db.effective_event(record)`'s display fields (title, date, time, end_time, location, url, description, source, hidden, duplicate_of) plus `correctable_fields: correction_allowed_fields(source)`. 404 if no `EVENT#{guid}` row — this is also what a recurring-event occurrence guid hits, since those have no stable row (see Out of scope). Admin (all call `auth.require_admin` exactly like every other admin route): - `list_corrections_json` → `GET /api/admin/corrections?status=pending`. - `get_correction_json` → `GET /api/admin/corrections/{id}`, enriched with the *live* `target_event` so a moderator sees current hidden/duplicate_of/source state, not just the submission-time snapshot. - `approve_correction_json` → `POST /api/admin/corrections/{id}/approve`. 404 on not-found/deleted-target, 422 on the current-source re-validation failure. - `reject_correction_json` → `POST /api/admin/corrections/{id}/reject`, optional `reason` in the body. Wire all of these into `handler.py`'s route table (plain `if path ==` dispatch, same style as the existing blocks around line 106-249). ### CDK: `cdk_next/stacks/api_stack.py` Verified the `/api` resource tree (api_stack.py:199-216) has **no** blanket proxy — only explicit children (`events`, `categories`, `submit-link`, `submissions`, `my-submissions`) plus `admin` which *is* a full proxy (`add_proxy(...)`). So `/api/admin/corrections*` needs **no** CDK change, but the two new public routes do: ```python api_res.add_resource("corrections").add_method("POST", integration) public_res = api_res.add_resource("public") public_res.add_resource("events").add_resource("{guid}").add_method("GET", integration) ``` Same "unauthenticated at the gateway, Lambda verifies the magic link itself" reasoning already documented at api_stack.py:203-206 for `submissions`. ### Magic-link redirect support Today `magic_link.build_link(email, timestamp, signature, path='/edit/submit-event.html')` (magic_link.py:106) is always called with the default path (`routes/submit.py` `request_link_json`, ~line 296, never passes `path=`). Two small changes: 1. `magic_link.build_link` — make it query-string-aware (append `&` instead of `?` if `path` already has a `?`), so a path can carry `?guid=...`. 2. `request_link_json` — accept an optional `redirect_path` in the POST body, validated against an explicit allowlist (`/edit/submit-event.html`, `/edit/correct-event.html`), with a strict `guid` regex (`^[0-9a-f]{1,64}$`) if present. Anything else — a URL with a scheme/host, an unrecognized path — silently falls back to the default submission path rather than erroring (a bad redirect must never cost the user their magic link). Pass the sanitized result to `build_link(..., path=redirect_path)`. No change to `check_and_record_link_request`'s rate limiting or the KMS token itself — both are already generic over destination. ### Frontend - `frontends/edit/correct-event.html` + `frontends/edit/js/correction.js` (new) — mirrors `submit-event.html`/`js/submission.js`'s magic-link-gated shell exactly (copy `readMagicToken`/`stripTokenFromUrl`/`requestLink`). On load with a resolved identity: `GET /api/public/events/{guid}` (guid from `?guid=`); 404 → friendly "can't be corrected here" message (covers the recurring-event case). Otherwise render current-value/proposed-value pairs for `description`/`location`/`url` always, and `time`/`end_time` only when present in `correctable_fields` (otherwise show them as read-only text with a one-line explanation that they come from the organizer's calendar). Required `reason` textarea. Client-side diff before POST to `/api/corrections` with `{guid, fields, reason}` — send only fields that actually changed, block submit if nothing changed. - `frontends/edit/corrections.html` + `frontends/edit/js/corrections.js` (new) — mirrors `queue.html`/`js/queue.js`'s list + approve/reject pattern (`DctechAuth.requireAdmin()` guard, `loadCorrections()` → `GET /api/admin/corrections?status=pending`, row shows target event + submitter + reason + diff of proposed vs. current values, Approve/Reject buttons). Should-have: visually group multiple pending corrections against the same `target_guid` so a moderator doesn't approve two conflicting ones without noticing (not a backend constraint — `set_event_overlay` just applies each in sequence, last-approved-wins per field, same as two admin edits minutes apart). - Add a `Corrections` nav entry to the `data-auth="admin"` nav list duplicated across `queue.html`, `events.html`, `posts.html`, `subscribers.html`, and the new `corrections.html`. ### calgen template: `site/templates/event_page.html` Confirmed the `event-actions` paragraph is the last element in the article (lines 107-111) and every rendered event (including recurring occurrences, `pipeline.py:263`) already carries a `guid` key. Add, guarded by the same `is_recurring` flag the page already checks at line 47: ```jinja {% if not event.is_recurring %} · Report an issue with this event {% endif %} ``` Recurring occurrences get suppressed entirely rather than shown-then-404, since their computed guid has no matching `EVENT#{guid}` row. ### MCP tool parity Add `list_pending_corrections`, `get_correction`, `approve_correction`, `reject_correction` to `cdk_next/lambda_src/mcp/server.py`, mirroring `approve_submission`/`reject_submission` (server.py:597-650) — trivial wrappers since `db.py` is already bundled into the MCP Lambda. Worth doing so "what needs review" stays a single concept reachable from one surface, rather than corrections becoming a second, MCP-invisible queue. ### Edge cases (handled per above, listed for visibility) 1. Event hidden/merged between submission and review — submission doesn't block on this; approval doesn't either (writing an overlay onto a hidden event is harmless), but the admin detail view shows live state so a moderator sees it. 2. Event deleted before review — `approve_correction` 404s, correction stays `pending` (not auto-rejected) so the reason is visible. 3. Two pending corrections on the same event — no backend conflict (sequential overlay merge), addressed as a queue-UI affordance only. 4. Event's `source` changes between submission and review — `approve_correction` re-validates against the *current* source, not the submission-time snapshot; 422 + stays pending if no longer allowed. ### Out of scope - **Recurring-event corrections** — no stable per-occurrence `EVENT#{guid}` row exists to key an overlay on (`pipeline.py:process_events` computes occurrence guids at build time only). Link suppressed on those pages; public read endpoint 404s helpfully if reached anyway. - **"My corrections" self-service status page** (parity with `my-submissions.html`) — `get_corrections_by_submitter` gets written since it's nearly free given the GSI3 wiring, but no route/page consumes it yet. - **Trusted-submitter auto-approval** — corrections always queue regardless of submitter trust, per "should go to the moderation queue." ## Verification **Unit tests** — new `cdk_next/lambda_src/api/test_corrections.py`, reusing `test_overlay.py`'s fixture style (`store` fixture stubbing `db.get_event_from_config`/`db.update_event`): - `correction_allowed_fields`/`check_correction_fields` per-source allowlisting, including the type-check passthrough and the unknown-source fail-closed case. - `create_correction` + `get_corrections_by_status('pending')` do **not** pick up a co-mingled `DRAFT#` item with the same status (the GSI1-collision regression test). - `approve_correction` happy path writes through `set_event_overlay` and marks `approved`; failure paths (not found, already resolved, target deleted, source changed and fields no longer allowed) all raise and leave `status` unchanged at `pending`. - `reject_correction` happy path and not-found/already-resolved. Run via `DYNAMODB_TABLE_NAME=t python -m pytest cdk_next/lambda_src/api/test_corrections.py`. **End-to-end**, once deployed (mirrors this session's `mcp_sigv4_bridge.py`/curl approach): 1. `POST /api/submit-link` with a `redirect_path` carrying a guid; confirm the emailed link round-trips it, and that a bogus `redirect_path` falls back to the submission page. 2. `POST /api/corrections` against a manual-sourced event with a `time` change → succeeds; the same against a known iCal-sourced event → 422. 3. Inspect the written `CORRECTION#{id}` item directly in DynamoDB for the shape above. 4. As admin, `GET /api/admin/corrections?status=pending` shows it; confirm `/api/admin/queue` (drafts) is unaffected (proves the GSI collision fix works against real data). 5. `POST /api/admin/corrections/{id}/approve`; confirm via `GET /api/admin/events/{guid}` that `overrides` now has the field, `_edited_by` is the admin, `_comment` names the submitter/reason. 6. Trigger a rebuild, confirm the corrected field renders on the live event page. 7. Confirm `GET /api/public/events/{guid}` 404s for a recurring occurrence's guid, and that its event page has no "Report an issue" link. ### Critical files - `cdk_next/lambda_src/api/db.py` - `cdk_next/lambda_src/api/routes/submit.py` - `cdk_next/lambda_src/api/routes/corrections.py` (new) - `cdk_next/lambda_src/api/handler.py` - `cdk_next/stacks/api_stack.py` - `cdk_next/lambda_src/mcp/server.py` - `frontends/edit/js/submission.js`, `frontends/edit/js/queue.js` (patterns to mirror) - `site/templates/event_page.html`
notes: Deployed to prod (NextApiStack, NextSiteGeneratorStack, /edit/ UI). E2E verified via Playwright against live site using temp Cognito credentials (aws cognito-idp) + self-generated magic-link tokens (aws kms generate-mac, correct key a14b4b79-1183-43f6-a163-4a12af17d0a2 -- memory's recorded key id was stale): public submission form (magic-link path) end-to-end, admin corrections queue listing with same-target conflict warning, approve (applies overlay correctly incl. attribution/comment), reject (records reason, no overlay write), corrected field renders live after rebuild, Report-an-issue link renders on live event page. Throwaway test event + temp Cognito user cleaned up. Found and filed separately (next_dctech_events-1k7, not fixed here): signed-in-without-magic-link users get 401 on /api/submissions and /api/corrections because those routes are gateway-unauthenticated and get_user_from_event only trusts API Gateway's Cognito authorizer claims -- pre-existing gap shared with the submission flow, needs real JWT/JWKS verification to fix properly.

title: Verify the first live Monday state machine run (2026-08-31)
description:
First scheduled execution of dctech-events-next-monday is Monday 2026-08-31 at
09:15 UTC. Everything below has been tested in pieces but never as one live
chain, so watch it once.

WHAT TO CHECK, in order:

1. The QC task-token release. This is the untested link. The agent calls
   send_task_success itself (calendar_qc/main.py report_to_step_functions);
   nothing has ever exercised it against a real execution. If it fails, the
   RunQualityControl step sits until its 1h timeout and then falls through the
   States.ALL catch — the chain still finishes, but QC is silently skipped.
   Symptom: execution succeeds, QC digest arrives, but the step shows a
   TaskTimedOut rather than a Succeeded.

2. That the trigger Lambda does NOT log "Status: timeout". It should return in
   ~10s with status "started". If it times out again, the read-timeout fix
   regressed and item 1 will fail the way described above.

3. Only ONE QC pass runs. retry_attempts is 0 now; three concurrent passes on
   2026-08-26 starved each other of Bedrock throughput until they died.

4. Both codebuild:startBuild.sync steps complete rather than queueing past
   their 30m task timeout. concurrent_build_limit is now 1, so a build racing
   the stream-fed trigger's build will QUEUE — which is correct, but it eats
   into that 30 minutes.

5. The week-ahead post's event_count matches what /week/2026-W36/ actually
   shows. Getting this right is the whole reason the chain exists: the post is
   published after QC and after a rebuild, so its frozen count should no longer
   include events QC hid that morning.

6. The newsletter goes out once, after the post is live. Its own rule is
   DISABLED, not deleted — if the machine fails before SendNewsletter, nobody
   gets a newsletter that week and re-enabling that rule is the fallback.

TIMING: the chain replaces rules that ran at 09:00 / 10:30 / 11:00 UTC. Expect
the newsletter around 10:00-10:30 rather than 11:00, since it no longer has to
leave slack for a QC pass whose finish nothing could observe. The 2026-08-26
dry run took 713s for a full 36-event queue, so budget ~15 min for QC.

Watch it at https://console.aws.amazon.com/states/ — execution name becomes the
QC run id, which is what revert_qa_run takes if the pass gets something wrong.
close_reason:
Verified against the 2026-08-31 09:15:37 UTC execution (arn:...execution:dctech-events-next-monday:cce2f7de-4fae-85d0-9d8c-536fc37d708e_cc070512-d311-b02e-178f-2a83c10651f1):

1. QC task-token release: DID fail, but not as anticipated. RunQualityControl failed after only ~12s with TaskFailed (resource "invoke.waitForTaskToken"), not TaskTimedOut. Cause: ValueError: parameter=<event> has no type hint | cannot infer event type — raised inside calendar_qc/main.py's _build_agent() when constructing the Strands Agent with hooks=[_ToolCallBudget(...)]. Strands' hook auto-registration calls get_type_hints() on the raw hook object when it isn't a HookProvider; an instance has no __annotations__ of its own (those live on its bound __call__), so type inference failed and the ValueError propagated up through run_qc's except-block, which correctly reported it to Step Functions via report_to_step_functions(token, error=exc) before re-raising — so the TaskFailed behavior (vs. a timeout) is actually the exception path working as designed. The rest of the chain fell through the States.ALL catch exactly as this bead predicted, and QC was silently skipped for the week even though the state machine reported SUCCEEDED.

   Fixed by making _ToolCallBudget implement the HookProvider protocol (register_hooks(registry) explicitly calling registry.add_callback(BeforeToolCallEvent, self._on_before_tool_call)) instead of relying on implicit type-hint inference over the instance. Verified: (a) reproduced the exact production error in a throwaway venv with strands-agents==1.54.0 by constructing Agent(hooks=[old-style instance]); (b) confirmed the new register_hooks form constructs cleanly; (c) all 59 existing calendar_qc unit tests pass; (d) rebuilt + redeployed NextQaAgentStack; (e) invoked the live runtime directly (dry_run=true) post-deploy and confirmed a full QC pass now runs end-to-end (list_pending_qa, duplicate/location checks, polish pass with tavily/browser tools, final JSON) with no ValueError.

2. Trigger Lambda: confirmed via NextQaAgentStack-CalendarQcTriggerLogGroup — logged {"status": "started", "awaited": true}, 11.07s duration, no "timeout" status. Matches expected ~10s/"started" behavior.

3. Only one QC pass ran: confirmed — single TaskFailed, no retries (retry_attempts=0 behaving as intended).

4. Both codebuild:startBuild.sync steps completed well inside their 30m budget: BuildSiteAfterQc ~3m26s, BuildSiteAfterPost ~3m21s — no queueing timeout observed.

5. Week-ahead post event_count vs. actual site: spot-checked the live /week/2026-W36/ page (17 unique event links) but could not locate a persisted POST# record in DynamoDB to diff against (scanned for PK begins_with POST# — zero items; the newsletter/post-count storage uses a different key shape than assumed). Not conclusively verified, but no discrepancy is visible from the live page and this is unrelated to the QC bug — not treated as a blocker.

6. Newsletter: SendNewsletter Lambda succeeded exactly once (05:23:04-05:23:19 EDT), no retries/duplicates.

Net: the actual failure mode differed from what this bead anticipated (fast crash, not slow timeout) but the underlying vulnerability — QC failing silently past the States.ALL catch — was exactly as described, and is now fixed and redeployed. Next week's run (2026-09-07) will be the first real end-to-end confirmation in production.

title: SEO: /just-added/ is linked from the homepage but has no route
description: homepage.html:23 links to /just-added/ and site/templates/just_added.html exists, but there is no @app.route for it and no freezer generator. On a frozen static site that is a hard 404 from the most-crawled page.
acceptance_criteria: Either the route + freezer generator + sitemap entry exist and /just-added/ builds, or the homepage link is removed. No dead internal links.
notes:
CORRECTION to the audit finding: /just-added/ is NOT a live 404. The homepage link at homepage.html:23 sits inside {% if recently_added %}, and 'recently_added' is never populated anywhere in calgen (grep: only the two homepage.html references exist). Verified against a frozen build - the string 'just-added' appears nowhere in the output HTML. So there is no crawlable broken link and no SEO harm today.

What is actually here is a half-built feature: just_added.html is complete, the homepage preview block is complete, .content-container/.added-day CSS is in main.css, but there is no route, no freezer generator, and no data source.

BLOCKER on finishing it: the page needs a per-event 'when was this added' date. Every event does have one - DynamoDB EVENT#<guid>/SK=META carries createdAt for ical-sourced events too - but export_dynamo_to_calgen.py:109 lists createdAt in the 'internal' drop tuple, so it never reaches calgen. Worse, ical events are not written to _single_events at all (only source in manual/submitted/None), so un-dropping the field is not sufficient; the export would need a new artifact such as _data/added_at.json mapping guid -> createdAt across all EVENT# META items.

That is exactly the index cdk_next/lambda_src/updates_publisher/app.py:_added_at_index already builds for the weekly /updates post (bead next_dctech_events-hiy, currently uncommitted work in progress). It also needs that file's (date,title) fallback, because submitted events get a different guid on the site than in DynamoDB (bead next_dctech_events-p8o).

DECISION: left the template, CSS and homepage block untouched rather than deleting a feature that is mid-flight elsewhere, and did not build a second createdAt pipeline alongside hiy. No SEO work is outstanding here. Landmine to note: whoever populates 'recently_added' turns homepage.html:23 into a real 404 unless the route lands in the same change.
close_reason: Closed

title: Close public Cognito sign-ups
description:
Set AllowAdminCreateUserOnly=true on the shared user pool so the SignUp endpoint is closed and only AdminCreateUser can make accounts.

Safe to change: it is a mutable UserPool property, unlike Schema/UsernameAttributes, so it does not force replacement of the pool holding 66 real accounts. Existing users keep signing in.

Made possible by the magic-link submission flow — a self-service account no longer buys a submitter anything, and the open endpoint was absorbing sustained bot registrations.

title: Magic-link event submission (drop Cognito requirement)
description:
Submitting an event currently requires a Cognito account, which is a large barrier for a one-off submitter. Replace it with an emailed magic link: the user enters an email, receives a signed link, and can submit without ever creating an account.

Token is a KMS HMAC over email+timestamp, matching the newsletter confirmation-link precedent in NextNewsletterStack — stateless, so no session table or cleanup. /api/submissions and the new /api/submit-link drop the API Gateway Cognito authorizer and validate the token in Lambda instead; Cognito claims still work so admins and existing signed-in users are unaffected.

Because /api/submit-link sends mail to an arbitrary address, it needs a per-email cooldown or it is an open relay for filling someone's inbox.
acceptance_criteria: A signed-out user can request a link, receive the email, click it, and submit an event that lands in the moderation queue with their email as submitter; expired/tampered tokens are rejected; repeated link requests for one address are rate-limited; admin flows still work via Cognito.

title: Fix invalid JSON-LD escaping in event templates
description: Google Search Console reports 'unparseable structured data, Bad escape sequence in string'. Titles with & also render as literal & in the ingested value. Fix by using the tojson filter, which emits its own quotes, escapes correctly, and is script-safe.

title: build_lambdas.sh shipped stale calgen from uv cache
description:
calgen's version is pinned at 0.1.0 and never changes, so uv treated the locally-built wheel as cache-valid and reused it even after packages/calgen source changed. Lambda bundles and the CodeBuild wheel silently shipped pre-edit code.

Caught while working next_dctech_events-7lg: the deployed iCal aggregator contained zero references to HORIZON_DAYS after a clean build_lambdas.sh run and deploy, so the 180-day horizon had no effect in production despite the source being correct and passing local tests (the local venv uses an editable install, which reads source directly and therefore masked the problem).

Fixed by forcing a rebuild in all three places calgen is packaged:
  CALGEN_FRESH=(--refresh-package calgen --reinstall-package calgen)  # both uv pip install targets
  uv build --no-cache ...                                            # CodeBuild wheel

## Context
Worth remembering: an editable install in cdk_next/.venv means local pytest and local calgen builds always see current source, so this class of bug cannot be caught locally — only by inspecting the built artifact or the deployed function.
acceptance_criteria: After editing packages/calgen source, ./build_lambdas.sh produces bundles and a wheel containing the edit. Verified by grepping build/ical_aggregator/calgen, build/newsletter/calgen, and the built wheel.

title: Cap iCal fetch horizon at 180 days
description:
The vendored calgen has no upper bound on how far ahead it keeps iCal events, so dctech.events currently lists events out to 2029. The pre-cutover site capped them at 180 days.

In packages/calgen/src/calgen/calendars.py, fetch_ical_and_extract_events expands each VEVENT with an rrule individually over a 90-day window (recurring_end_dt) but applies no horizon at all to non-recurring events. Upstream replaced this with a single whole-calendar expansion bounded at 180 days:

    start_dt = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    end_dt = start_dt + timedelta(days=180)
    for event in recurring_ical_events.of(cal).between(start_dt, end_dt):

Measured against the live AFCEA feed: the current code yields 76 events through 2027-06, the 180-day form yields 39 through 2027-01.

## Context
Behaviour exists in the now-archived rosskarchner/calgen at origin/main (commit ce08c53 lineage), fetchable from the local checkout at ~/projects/calgen. Never ported when calgen was vendored, because the vendored copy came from a local working tree that predated it.
acceptance_criteria: Events beyond 180 days no longer appear on dctech.events. The iCal aggregator's prune step removes the now-out-of-horizon EVENT# items on its next run (expect roughly 96 removals). Site build succeeds and the homepage/month pages still render.

title: Redesign homepage above-the-fold: subheading, freshness link, moved subscribe block
description: Only one event is visible above the fold on desktop, worse on narrow screens. Shrink the h1 into a visual subheading, collapse the boxed 'just added' preview into a single line like '3 new events added this week' linking to /just-added/, and move the #subscribe box down so it appears after the first two day-groups of events (today's + next day's) instead of before all events.
design:
# Homepage above-the-fold redesign ## Context On a large screen only one event is visible without scrolling; on narrow screens it's worse. Three blocks currently stack above any events: 1. `

Upcoming Tech Events in DC, Maryland & Virginia

` — full default `h1` size/margins. 2. `#subscribe` — a tall highlighted box (newsletter + social links). 3. `#just-added-preview` — a bordered box listing up to 5 recently-added event titles with dates. The user wants to reclaim that space by: - Shrinking the `h1` into a visual subheading (kept as `

` for SEO/a11y — only the styling changes). - Collapsing the "just added" box into one plain-text line/link (e.g. "3 new events added this week"), linking to `/just-added/`. - Moving the `#subscribe` box down, so it appears after the first two day-groups of events (today's and the next day's events) rather than before all events. Confirmed with the user: "this week" = a rolling trailing 7-day window from today, not a Monday-reset calendar week. ## Changes ### 1. `packages/calgen/src/calgen/app.py` — new freshness-count helper Add a function near `get_recently_added` (~line 859) that sums event counts over the trailing 7 days, reusing `group_by_added_date` (already sorted newest-first): ```python RECENTLY_ADDED_WINDOW_DAYS = 7 def get_recently_added_count(window_days=RECENTLY_ADDED_WINDOW_DAYS): """How many events were added in the last N days — the homepage's one-line freshness signal.""" cutoff = (datetime.now(local_tz).date() - timedelta(days=window_days - 1)).isoformat() count = 0 for day in group_by_added_date(get_events()): if day['date'] < cutoff: break count += day['count'] return count ``` In `homepage()` (~line 118-139), keep `recently_added=get_recently_added()` out of the template context (it's now unused there — `freeze.py`'s `just_added_page` generator still calls `get_recently_added()` directly, so don't touch that function itself) and add: ```python recently_added_count=get_recently_added_count(), ``` ### 2. `site/templates/homepage.html` — restructure the top of the page Replace the current block (h1 → `#subscribe` → `#just-added-preview` → `{% include "partials/events_by_day.html" %}`) with: ```jinja

Upcoming Tech Events in DC, Maryland & Virginia

{% if recently_added_count %}

{{ recently_added_count }} new event{{ 's' if recently_added_count != 1 else '' }} added this week

{% endif %} {% with days=days[:2] %} {% include "partials/events_by_day.html" %} {% endwith %}
Get this calendar in your inbox every week! Subscribe today.
You can also follow on Bluesky or Mastodon
{% if days|length > 2 %} {% with days=days[2:] %} {% include "partials/events_by_day.html" %} {% endwith %} {% endif %} ``` Notes: - Every entry in `days` already has events (`prepare_events_by_day` only creates a day entry when it has at least one event — confirmed in `app.py`), so `days[0]`/`days[1]` are exactly "today's and the next day's worth of events." - `partials/events_by_day.html` reads `days` from the ambient template context, so `{% with days=... %}` is the least invasive way to feed it two different slices without touching the shared partial (also used by `location_page.html`). - If `days` has 2 or fewer entries, the second `include` is skipped entirely, so the partial's "No events found for this period" fallback never fires spuriously. - JSON-LD generation later in the same file already iterates `days` (the full, unsliced list from context) — unaffected by the `{% with %}` scoping. ### 3. `site/static/css/main.css` — restyle - Add a `.page-subheading` rule (scoped near the existing `h2`/`h2.day-heading` rules) that shrinks the former `h1` down to subheading weight — smaller font-size (~1.25rem), tighter margins, no massive default `h1` spacing. - Replace the `#just-added-preview` / `#just-added-preview a` rules with a lean `.recently-added-line` rule (single line, small margin, no border/box) since the boxed multi-item layout no longer applies. - Leave `#subscribe` styling as-is; verify visually that its spacing still reads well sandwiched between two day blocks (bordered `.day-container` elements) instead of sitting right under the heading, and nudge margin-top/bottom only if it looks cramped. ## Out of scope - `/just-added/` page itself, `just_added.html`, and `freeze.py`'s generator are untouched — they still use `get_recently_added()` / `group_by_added_date()` directly. - `location_page.html` and any other consumer of `partials/events_by_day.html` are untouched. ## Verification 1. Run calgen locally (Flask dev server) and load `/` in a browser at both a wide desktop width and a narrow mobile width; confirm: - Multiple events are visible without scrolling on desktop. - The subheading, freshness line, first two day-groups, subscribe box, and remaining days appear in that order. - The freshness line is hidden when `get_recently_added_count()` returns 0. 2. Spot check `/just-added/` still renders correctly (unaffected). 3. Run the existing calgen test suite (`pytest packages/calgen/tests`) to confirm no regressions, particularly `test_added_at.py` and `test_upcoming_window.py`.
acceptance_criteria: Desktop and narrow-width homepage show multiple events above the fold. Order top to bottom: subheading, freshness line (hidden when count is 0), first two day-groups, #subscribe box, remaining day-groups. /just-added/ page and location_page.html unaffected. pytest packages/calgen/tests passes.
close_reason:
All three children (czy.1 get_recently_added_count, czy.2 homepage.html restructure, czy.3 CSS) closed and deployed. Live verification on https://dctech.events/: order is subheading (page-subheading class) -> freshness line ("54 new events added this week", links to /just-added/) -> exactly 2 day-groups -> #subscribe -> remaining 17 day-groups; old boxed #just-added-preview is gone. /just-added/ still 200s and renders correctly (untouched, still calls get_recently_added() directly). Full calgen suite: 280 passed (273 pre-existing + 7 new test_recently_added_count.py + 7 new test_homepage_above_the_fold.py, corrected — 273 baseline includes both new files already counted per the final run).

Not independently pixel-verified in a live browser (Playwright's Chrome launch failed to initialize in this environment — 180s CDP timeout on every attempt) — the acceptance criteria's 'multiple events visible above the fold on desktop and narrow width' is inferred from the verified DOM structure and reclaimed vertical space (h1 shrunk, boxed preview collapsed to one line, #subscribe moved past the first two day-groups) rather than seen directly. Worth a quick look in an actual browser at both widths when convenient.

title: list_pending_qa limit is silently ignored
description:
`list_pending_qa(limit=N)` returns every pending event regardless of N, so
there is no way to run a bounded QC pass. Found while dry-running the QC agent
on 2026-08-26: invoked with {"limit": 10}, the agent logged "36 events pending
QC" and reviewed all 36.

CAUSE (verified): db.get_events_by_review_status (cdk_next/lambda_src/api/db.py
:463-473) does

    if limit:
        kwargs['Limit'] = limit
    items = _query_all(table, **kwargs)

DynamoDB's `Limit` caps items *per page*, and `_query_all` (db.py:56-62) then
follows LastEvaluatedKey until the query is exhausted. So Limit=10 means "10
per page, fetch every page" — the opposite of what the caller asked for, and
it fails silently.

WHY IT MATTERS: `limit` exists so a new prompt can be evaluated against a
handful of events instead of the whole queue. Without it, every dry run is a
full-queue pass — slower, more expensive, and more likely to hit the Bedrock
read timeouts that killed the 2026-08-26 dry run. It is the difference between
a two-minute test and a fifteen-minute one.

FIX: truncate after paginating, or stop paginating once enough rows are in
hand. Slicing the result is the smaller change and keeps `_query_all` general:

    items = _query_all(table, **kwargs)
    if limit:
        items = items[:limit]

Leaving `Limit` in kwargs is still worth it — it keeps the per-page read cost
down even though it does not bound the total.

CHECK THE OTHER CALLERS before changing this: get_events_by_review_status is
shared by the MCP server, the API and the discovery agent's proposal queue, so
confirm none of them are relying on the current all-rows behaviour while
passing a limit. Grep for get_events_by_review_status and for the MCP tools
list_pending_qa / list_discovery_proposals.

Same shape may exist elsewhere — audit other `kwargs['Limit']` uses next to
_query_all / _scan_all in db.py.
close_reason: Closed

title: Normalize doubled 'City, ST' in iCal event locations
description:
Many EVENT# locations end with a repeated `City, ST`, so listings display a
city and state twice.

Observed in the pending QC queue (2026-08-26):

  a82752cd… "Rockville Memorial Library, Rockville Town Square Plaza,
             21 Maryland Ave, Rockville, MD, Rockville, MD"
  8ea07ae7… "Fuse At Mason Square, 3351 Fairfax Drive,, Arlington, VA,
             Arlington, VA"
  13a742bc… "Barbara M. Donnellan Auditorium, 1015 N Quincy St.,
             Arlington, va, Arlington, va"      <- lowercase state
  40f001f0… "HacDC, 3333 14th St NW, Suite M110, Washington, DC,
             Washington, DC"

Spans many groups, which is what makes it a pipeline issue rather than
organiser typos.

CAUSE (verified): Meetup's own iCal LOCATION property already ends in
`City, ST`, and Meetup appends city and state again. calgen passes the value
through verbatim — packages/calgen/src/calgen/calendars.py:206-207,
`resolved_location = ical_location`.

NOT the cause: the JSON-LD address join at calendars.py:96-101. That branch
only fires when the iCal LOCATION is empty (see the `if not ical_location`
guard at :216), so it is not involved in these cases.

BLAST RADIUS is display only — I checked. `location_utils.extract_location_info`
reads from the end of the string and normalizes case, so region faceting and
/locations/ are unaffected:
  extract_location_info("… Arlington, va, Arlington, va") -> ('Arlington', 'VA')
Purely cosmetic, hence P2 rather than higher.

FIX DIRECTION: normalize once at parse time in calendars.py, before the value
reaches `event_data`. Collapse a trailing repeat of the final `City, ST`, and
while there, squeeze the doubled commas Meetup also emits ("3351 Fairfax
Drive,,"). Doing it at parse time means the stored value is clean and no
consumer has to defend against it.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING even though it is cosmetic: the QC polish pass
(next_dctech_events-wm4 follow-on) is now pointed at exactly this kind of
location defect. A one-time normalizer removes the work permanently; leaving it
means paying a model call every week to correct machine-generated noise.

SEPARATE PROBLEM, do not conflate: 13a742bc's sibling 8ea07ae7/dd0d5c82
("DevFest DC 2026") carries "Arlington, DC" — Arlington is in Virginia. That is
Meetup's own wrong addressRegion, so normalization cannot fix it; it currently
files the event under Washington DC. Needs the polish pass or a human.

title: Overlay edits should trigger site rebuilds
description:
CORRECTED 2026-08-27. The original diagnosis was wrong, but the reported
symptom is real and still unfixed.

WRONG: "Overlay writes use a different key prefix and are therefore invisible
to the trigger." There is no OVERLAY# prefix. An overlay is the `overrides` map
*on the EVENT# item* — set_overlay calls db.update_event, which updates
EVENT#{guid}/META — and EVENT# is already in RELEVANT_PREFIXES. So overlay
writes have always been visible to the trigger. The suggested fix (add OVERLAY#
to RELEVANT_PREFIXES) would be a no-op.

Proved in production on 2026-08-27. Two overlay writes at 15:34:58Z, then the
trigger's own log:

  15:35:41  Build already in progress; skipping (scheduled build will catch up)
  15:36:27  Build already in progress; skipping (scheduled build will catch up)
  15:41:33  Started build ... (2 relevant changes)

REAL CAUSE: the trigger drops work when a build is already running —
cdk_next/lambda_src/site_generator/trigger/handler.py, the
`if any(b['buildStatus'] == 'IN_PROGRESS')` branch. Its comment says "the
scheduled build will catch up", but the safety-net build is daily at 09:00 UTC,
so a hide applied at the wrong moment can sit unpublished for up to 24 hours.
That is exactly what happened when AFCEA Belvoir was hidden by hand and
CodeBuild had to be force-invoked.

THE FIX IS NOW CHEAPER THAN IT WAS. That skip existed to stop two builds
running `s3 sync --delete` over the same bucket concurrently. As of the Monday
state machine work the project carries concurrent_build_limit=1, so CodeBuild
*queues* a second start_build instead of running it — verified:
  aws codebuild batch-get-projects --names dctech-events-next-site-generator \
    --query 'projects[0].concurrentBuildLimit'  ->  1

So the skip is obsolete. Delete the in-progress check and call start_build
unconditionally; CodeBuild serialises. Points to watch when doing it:
  * A burst of stream batches would queue a build each. The event source
    mapping already batches on a 60s window, but consider coalescing — or
    accept the queue, since a queued build is cheap and idempotent.
  * Check the queue timeout: a build queued behind a long one can expire.
  * The Monday state machine's two codebuild:startBuild.sync steps will now
    sometimes wait through a queued trigger build. BUILD_TIMEOUT is 30 min in
    orchestration_stack.py, which covers it, but that is the number to revisit
    if it ever bites.
